texts: mixed: the warding event, "ward back" kept whole as one verb, the group of Keepers doing it, the wraith as what was warded, and the feathers as the means are all correct; the one bad atom is "ground", which lands on the bundle of feathers as a whole rather than on each feather, so "was this feather ground?" can never resolve. Moving the modifier into its own clause fixes it without changing what you are saying: "Keepers warded the wraith back with feathers that had been ground."

good. the opinion is recorded as every Keeper's own, the plan's dangerousness stays inside the belief (nothing asserts the plan really was dangerous), the past tense is kept there too, and the rule fires for any Keeper who turns up later.
